name: gap_fade_large_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Large gaps (>1.5%) in NIFTY 50 stocks are disproportionately caused by overnight sentiment over-reaction to global cues (US market moves, Asian open, commodity prices) rather than stock-specific news. When no earnings or corporate action drives the gap, large gaps fade (partially revert) 55-60% of the time because the overnight price impact overshoots the fundamental information content. The key insight is that Indian markets open 4-5 hours after US close, and overnight futures already priced in the US move — the cash market open often over-extends due to retail market orders at open. Fading the excess (the gap beyond what NIFTY futures implied) captures this over-reaction.
mechanism: Opening gaps trigger stop-loss cascades from overnight position holders, overshooting fair value. As the cascade exhausts, institutional VWAP algorithms begin working counter-gap orders, and fresh participants enter at the perceived discount or premium, driving price back toward the prior close or VWAP level within the first 15-30 minutes.

indicators.name: excess_gap
indicators.formula: gap_pct - NIFTY_implied_gap_pct  # stock gap beyond index gap

conditions: no earnings or corporate action for the stock today
no earnings or corporate action for the stock today

exit.signal_exit: if volume_climax fires in gap direction while in trade, exit (new institutional flow confirming gap)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; above 25, large gaps are often structural

weaknesses: The news filter is imperfect — sometimes gaps are driven by leaked information, off-market block deals, or global events that fundamentally justify the gap, leading to gap-and-go instead of fade
Low frequency: large gaps (>1.5%) occur on only ~15-20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring monitoring of the full NIFTY 50 universe for sufficient signals
Wider bid-ask spreads at open on gap days increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly eating into the edge vs normal days
prior_art: Dyl & Maberly (1992) gap reversal; Fabozzi et al. (2007) on overnight gap return predictability. Indian context similar to findings in Aggarwal & Gupta (2009) on NSE opening returns.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
